entry.title: Time Complexity & Big-O Notation Explained Simply
entry.summary:
Handling 10 inputs is easy. Handling 10 lakh inputs is where real skill shows. That's what time complexity measures. It measures how the number of operations grows as input size grows — not seconds, not milliseconds. function getFirst(arr) { return arr[0]; } // Always 1 step
function findMax(arr) { let max = arr[0]; for (let i = 1; i < arr.length; i++) { if (arr[i] > max) max = arr[i]; } return max; }
Each step halves the problem. 1,000,000 elements → only ~20 steps. Example: Binary search. for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { for (let j = 0; j < n; j++) { /* n×n ops */ } }
n O(1) O(log n) O(n) O(n²)
10 1 3 10 100
1,000 1 10 1,000 1,000,000
10,000 1 13 10,000 100,000,000
At 10,000 elements — O(n²) runs 100 million ops vs O(n)'s 10,000. Always analyse time complexity before and after optimising. Interviewers ask: "What's the Big-O?" Part 4 of the Bitveen DSA Series. Originally published at bitveen.com

entry.title: MCP Fetch SSRF Protection Checklist
entry.summary: A URL tool can reach whatever the MCP server can reach. If that server runs in a cloud, CI, laptop, VPC, or cluster, open fetch becomes a credential and internal-network boundary. The safe default is to deny dangerous targets before the request leaves the runtime. A fetch MCP server is not just a read tool. It is network egress running from wherever the agent host sits. SSRF protection has to run before the HTTP request: parse the URL, resolve DNS, classify every resolved address, apply redirect policy, and deny metadata, loopback, private, IPv6 ULA, and in-cluster targets by default. Most APIs in 2026 still ship the same artifacts they shipped in 2016: an OpenAPI spec, a SwaggerUI page, maybe a Postman collection if the team is feeling generous. Those are great for humans.
